title: Anthropic ends its first week worth $1.6tn as VCs count $25bn stakes
excerpt: ‘This is the largest I.P.O. in history, late in the A.I. cycle,’ one strategist said, as Anthropic IPO stock held above $83.
content_html:
Anthropic ended its first week of trading worth $1.6tn on a fully diluted basis, CNBC’s Jordan Novet reported on Saturday. Only six US companies are worth more: Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Nvidia, Amazon and SpaceX.

The shares closed at $88.91 on Friday, down 8.5% on the day. That gave back half of the 17% gain from its first day of trading. The stock still held above the $83 IPO price. The Nasdaq fell 10% over the week, its worst since the early days of Covid in 2020, CNBC reported.

Anthropic confirmed on Friday that it had closed the offering. It sold 1.127bn shares at $83, raising $93.5bn, of which $91.6bn went to the company. AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners bought another $26bn at the same price. That brings the total to the $119.5bn reported on Friday morning.

A $25bn windfall

At the IPO price, Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners each held about $25bn of Anthropic stock, CNBC reported. Bessemer Venture Partners held about $10bn, partner Byron Deeter said. Menlo was among the firms set to make more than 10 times their money.

“At the end of the day, that’s really our job, is to get dollars back into foundations and endowments,” Menlo’s Matt Murphy told CNBC.

Murphy said his firm had delivered more than $1bn in returns to each of more than five of its investors. In an April 2024 memo, Bessemer’s investors warned they could lose some or all of their money if Anthropic missed its targets, according to CNBC.

In the third quarter, Anthropic said, it made $1.72 in revenue for every dollar spent on computing power. A year earlier it made 68 cents. IVP general partner Somesh Dash told CNBC he hopes to see at least six AI companies list at valuations above $10bn each in late 2027.

Who paid more

Not everyone bought at $83. Many hedge funds missed out on the offering and paid $111.50 when trading opened on Thursday. That is according to AI industry analyst Raphaëlle D’Ornano, speaking to The New York Times’ Cory Weinberg. She called Friday “pure panic”.

Early employees sold more than $25bn of stock at the start of trading, the Times reported. Some investors and analysts saw that as aggressive. Companies usually stop insiders from selling for weeks or months after an IPO. Anthropic let staff sell 10% on day one.

“This is the largest I.P.O. in history, late in the A.I. cycle. Psychologically, that could be a topping event,” JonesTrading chief market strategist Michael O’Rourke told the Times.

The risk in the research notes

Seaport Research Partners analyst Jay Goldberg added an unusual risk to his note on 18 November, CNBC’s Eric Rosenbaum reported.

“Anthropic could develop AI systems which become fully autonomous and wipe out humanity which may lead to a serious decline in earnings,” Goldberg wrote.

Goldman Sachs’ Panic Index has reached 9 out of 10, Bloomberg’s Natalia Kniazhevich said on Bloomberg This Weekend.

Amodei heads to Italy

Chief executive Dario Amodei is on holiday at a luxury resort in southern Italy, Bloomberg’s Daniele Lepido and Tiago Ramos Alfaro reported, citing people familiar with the matter. His private jet landed in Brindisi, in Puglia, at midday on Friday. The people said he plans to stay a few days. Anthropic declined to comment.
